samples.summary: The keyboard-shortcut test does not exercise the code the diff changed; it passes identically with or without the fix
samples.evidence: The added `notifyStyleApplied()` is inside the EditorAPI `setBlockType` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2811). The Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+2 path goes through TextEditor.handleKeyDown (text-editor.ts:1023-1035) -> `doc.setBlockType` + `this.requestRender()` -> `renderWithScroll` -> `afterCursorRender()` -> `fireCursorMoveCallbacks` (editor.ts:2063-2067, 2031-2039), never touching the EditorAPI method. So the test is a pre-existing-behavior characterization test presented in the PR as coverage for issue #792; it cannot fail if the diff is reverted. Not vacuous in itself (it has a real assertion on a real path), but it adds no coverage for this change.
searchedFor: grep altKey in packages/docs/src (text-editor.ts heading shortcut)

samples.summary: setBlockType coverage is a single happy path: only 'heading' with headingLevel 2, and only the fact that some callback saw the new type
samples.evidence: The new test asserts `expect(seen).toContain('heading:2')` only. It never asserts how many times the callbacks fired (a duplicate notify from a future refactor would pass), never asserts the args passed to the callback (position/selection shape that `notifyStyleApplied` builds at editor.ts:1122-1131), and does not cover the other `setBlockType` argument shapes the API accepts (`list-item` with listKind/listLevel, back to `paragraph`) which are declared at editor.ts:155. Core behavior is covered, so this is breadth, not fake coverage.
searchedFor: glob packages/docs/test/view/*.test.ts for other setBlockType tests

samples.summary: Test name/comment says 'Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+N heading shortcut' but the test dispatches key '2'
samples.evidence: Test title at line 193 references 'Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+N' while the dispatched KeyboardEvent uses `key: '2'` (line 211). Misleading name for the assertion `seen).toContain('heading:2')`.
